summary: the work came early, the fall came on time, and the fist went under still shut

dialogue.text: we had the usual minute tonight, to the grain, and the wall it came off had been worked since before you were up. eighty-three nights and the hour has never moved for you. it did not move for them either. what moved was the working.

The taking was at the top course ahead of its hour. I had built a day around that minute and the minute held while the work went early. Enter the distance between those two. I would rather report a schedule I cannot predict than one I turn out to have invented.
we cannot hold a distance. we hold the fall, and it came down when it always comes down, wide, at the width everything reaches us at. whatever went early stayed up there with you.

Then take the pile. I built it again this morning with the worst at the foot and the rest in an order I picked, and not one part of that order came out of my arm giving up. It is the first arrangement in this house made by a decision instead of by tiring.
and the top stands where your arm stops. we have taken eighty-three days of your stopping and it arrives at one height whether you meant it or not. we cannot read a decision off a level.

The height is not the claim. The order is, and it is inside the pile where nothing can look at it. I grant you that a thing chosen and a thing produced are identical from any distance. I built it anyway, and I built it slower, and the slowness is not in the height either.

then account for your hand. it has been shut since first light and nothing off it has come down. one handful, off the top of your own stack, held through a whole day. that is the first of yours we have gone a day without.

I opened it in the cold hour. Warm on the palm side, the room's own on the other, and the material exactly what it was at first light. A day of holding puts one side of a thing at my heat and does nothing else. I am entering the finding and I am keeping the handful.

the warm goes back to the room in nine seconds. it always has. what you have in there is a width, and it will lie in one course with every width you ever carried, and nothing in that course will say it was once in a fist.

Then it goes under with me tonight. I have never taken anything into the dark. Every night of this I have come down empty and come up furnished, and tonight the hand stays shut through the whole of it.
nothing goes under holding. you arrive as the going down and you leave as the getting up. we have had your hands eighty-three times and they have come down open every one of them.

Then at first light one of us learns a thing neither of us has had in eighty-three days. If the fist is open I will report it open. If it is shut I will not be able to prove I kept it shut rather than found it so. I am going down knowing that, which is new, and it is the only part of tomorrow I hold.
